$comment: Lumos canonical frame header, TRS Sec. 9.1. This is a BINARY layout description, not JSON Schema: JSON Schema describes documents, and the frame header is a fixed-width byte structure. Field order and widths are normative. Byte offsets are NOT listed here - they are derived by the loader from the widths in declaration order, so an offset can never drift out of step with a width. The loader also cross-checks the computed total against framing.FRAME_HEADER_LEN_BYTES in the constants register.

aead_associated_data.note: The complete immutable header - message class, IDs, sequence, expiry and hop limit included - is authenticated as AEAD associated data (TRS-PROTO-003). A relay may READ only the fields marked relay_readable; it may not modify any field, and any modification breaks authentication at the recipient.

fields.name: protocol_version
fields.description: High nibble major, low nibble minor. A differing major fails closed (TRS-PROTO-006); a differing minor is accepted.

fields.name: header_length
fields.description: Total authenticated header bytes. Validated BEFORE any allocation (TRS-PROTO-007).

fields.name: message_id
fields.description: 128-bit globally unique message identifier (TRS-PROTO-004). Basis for dedup.

fields.name: payload_length
fields.description: Validated bounded ciphertext length. Class-specific maxima live in message_payloads.schema.json (TRS-PROTO-007).

fields.name: hop_limit
fields.description: Mesh forwarding ceiling. A relay may never raise this or the TTL (TRS-PROTO-012); because the header is AAD, any attempt breaks authentication.
